title: Tensorization of norm contractions
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let each $\Omega_i$ be finite, and let $w_i:\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ and $k_i:\Omega_i\times\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative. Let $p,q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le p$ and $1<q$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and every $h:\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$, $\left(\sum_y w_i(y)\left|\sum_x k_i(y,x)h(x)\right|^q\right)^{1/q}\le\left(\sum_xw_i(x)|h(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}$. Then for every real-valued $f$ on $\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\left(\sum_y\left(\prod_iw_i(y_i)\right)\left|\sum_x\left(\prod_i k_i(y_i,x_i)\right)f(x)\right|^q\right)^{1/q}\le\left(\sum_x\left(\prod_iw_i(x_i)\right)|f(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}$.
hypotheses_covered: Each coordinate set Ω_i is finite
The stated one-coordinate norm inequality holds for every coordinate and every real-valued function on that coordinate set
f is real-valued on the product of the coordinate sets
replaced: Let $\Omega_i$ be finite sets, $w_i(a)\ge0$ weights, and $k_i(y,x)\ge0$ kernels for $i\in[n]$. For $p\ge1$ and $q>1$, suppose $\|\sum_xk_i(\,\cdot\,,x)h(x)\|_{q,w_i}\le\|h\|_{p,w_i}$ for every coordinate $i$ and real $h$. Then the product operator $Tf(y)=\sum_x\prod_i k_i(y_i,x_i)f(x)$ satisfies $\|Tf\|_{q,w}\le\|f\|_{p,w}$ for every real $f$ on $\prod_i\Omega_i$, with $w(x)=\prod_iw_i(x_i)$ and $\|h\|_{s,w}=(\sum_xw(x)|h(x)|^s)^{1/s}$.
